unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: This is the last unit of Year 2, and it gathers up everything you have learned. You revise thirty words from Units 1 to 9, from name and neighbour to butterfly, hut and underground, and you work through six grammar workshops that bring back pronouns, questions, commands, comparisons, There is and There are, and the past, present and future. Then you plan, draft, revise and publish an illustrated six-page booklet called My English World, and you present it at the class showcase just as Amal does in this unit's story.
unit.learningPath:
Read Amal's English Year, the project brief and the Showcase Day dialogue, then answer the twelve comprehension questions.
Revise the thirty review words in the nine unit groups and build your own word bank.
Complete the six cumulative grammar workshops, one for each pattern of the year.
Plan, draft, revise, edit and publish the six-page My English World booklet.
If you have access to live teacher sessions, rehearse in them and deliver your two-minute showcase presentation there — this is optional. If you are learning independently, rehearse and record your two-minute showcase presentation on your own or with your family instead.
Finish with the cumulative quiz, the portfolio assignment and your final reflection.
howToUse: This is your capstone: one big project that uses everything you learned this year. There is no video — start by reading about the project.
In Writing you make your own six-page booklet, “My English World”: plan it, write it, make it better, then publish it.
In Speaking you practise a two-minute showcase talk. If you have no live sessions, record it on your own or with your family.
The Final course quiz is on this page, after every section has a tick. It is extra — it does not lock the unit.

readings.title: Amal's English Year
readings.theme: Looking back on a year of learning
readings.setting: A Grade 2 classroom on the last two weeks of Year 2
readings.passageScript:
Amal opened her English folder on the last Monday of Year 2. At the front she found her welcome card from Unit 1. Her name was written in careful blue letters. Behind it lay a poem about her neighbour Theo. Next to the poem was a drawing of Leila the firefighter.

Amal turned another page. She found her shadow chart from the big sky unit. She found a measuring table and a bug fact file. She found her garden promise as well. Last of all she found her city map from Unit 9.

Teacher Yasmin smiled at the class. “This term you will build one last project,” she said. “It is called My English World.” Every child had to choose six pages from at least four different units.

Amal read her old work again. She fixed one sentence on her helpers page. She had written “The firefighters is working.” Now she wrote “The firefighters are working.” She added two describing words to her sky page. Unit 4 had taught her about adjectives.

Then Amal made her new booklet. Page one told the reader her name and her class. Page two showed a helpful neighbour. Page three showed the parts of the body. Page four showed the sun and a long shadow. Page five showed her house. Page six showed the library in the city.

On showcase day Amal stood beside her table. Her hands felt cold, so she breathed slowly. “Welcome to my English world,” she said. Nora and Leo listened, and Grandma Hana clapped.

At the end Amal wrote one last reflection. “I can read, write and speak more clearly now,” she wrote. “Next year I want to read a long chapter book.” She closed her folder and felt proud.

readings.title: The My English World Project Brief
readings.theme: Planning, making and presenting a booklet
readings.setting: The classroom noticeboard and the online capstone page
readings.passageScript:
My English World is your last project of Year 2, and Teacher Yasmin gives every class the same brief on the first Monday of the term. It has four parts, and you work through them in order, just like Amal did with her own booklet.

Part 1: Choose your pages. Pick six pages from at least four different units. Look for work that shows reading, writing, speaking and new words. Amal chose a page about a helpful neighbour, a page about the parts of the body, a page about the sun and shadows, and a page about the library in the city. She read through her old work first, so she picked her strongest pages instead of her newest ones.

Part 2: Make the booklet. Write two full sentences on every page, add one picture, and add one label. A label can be a single word, like butterfly or shadow, pointing at the exact part of your picture it describes. Keep your sentences simple and clear, the way you have all year: one main idea in every sentence, and a full stop at the end.

Part 3: Present your work. Speak for about two minutes at the class showcase. Point at your pictures as you talk, and answer one question from a listener. Practise out loud three times before showcase day, even if nobody else is in the room. Your own voice, heard again and again, is one of the best teachers you have.

Part 4: Reflect. Write three sentences about what you can do now that you could not do at the start of Year 2. Then write one goal for Year 3, such as reading a longer book or writing a longer story.

Read every page aloud before you hand it in. Your ears will find the missing full stops faster than your eyes will. If a partner or an adult is nearby, ask for one kind idea and one careful question about your work; if nobody is free, read it aloud to yourself instead and listen for any sentence that sounds unfinished. Fix what needs fixing, and keep the pages that are already strong. When your booklet is ready, you will be ready too.

readings.title: Showcase Day
readings.setting: The Grade 2 English showcase in the school hall
readings.passageScript:
Teacher Yasmin: Welcome, everybody, to our end-of-year showcase. A whole year of work fills this hall today, so take your time and look closely. Amal, would you like to present first?
Amal: Yes, please. Hello, my name is Amal, and my booklet is called My English World.
Teacher Yasmin: Lovely. Which page are you most proud of, Amal?
Amal: Page four. It shows the sun and my long shadow. Unit 4 taught me why shadows grow longer in the evening, so I drew mine at three different times of day.
Nora: I like your bug page too. The butterfly has beautiful wings.
Amal: Thank you, Nora. I labelled the wings and the antennae, and I coloured every wing a different pattern.
Theo: What about your neighbour page? I remember you asked me two questions for it.
Amal: I did! You told me you water our plants when we are away, so I used that as my example sentence.
Theo: I am glad it made the final six pages.
Leo: How did you make the plant page better?
Amal: I read it aloud to Adam. He said it was too short, so I added two facts about planting.
Teacher Yasmin: That is careful work, Amal. It shows real listening, and real revising. What is your goal for next year?
Amal: I want to read a long chapter book by myself, from the first page to the last.
Teacher Yasmin: A wonderful goal. Thank you, Amal. Nora, would you like to present next?
Nora: Yes, Teacher Yasmin. My booklet is called Nora's Word Journey, and my favourite page is the library page.
Teacher Yasmin: Wonderful. Everyone, please clap for Amal before we continue.
Teacher Yasmin: Thank you all for listening so carefully today. Remember, a good audience asks kind questions and waits for a full answer, just like Nora, Theo and Leo did for Amal.

grammar.title: Pronouns and Likes (Units 1 and 9)
grammar.explanation: In Unit 1 you learned to use he, she and they so that you do not repeat a name in every sentence. Use like with I, you, we and they, and use likes with he, she or one person's name.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Amal presents her booklet. She points at page four.
Leo and Sami wait their turn. They clap for Amal.
Amal likes her bug page. Her friends like the city map.
Grandma Hana likes the shadow drawing.
grammar.commonMistake: Some children write “Amal like her booklet.” One person needs likes, so the sentence becomes “Amal likes her booklet.”
grammar.memoryTip: One person takes the s: he likes, she likes. Two or more people drop it: we like, they like.
grammar.practice:

1. Nora finished her booklet. Nora is proud of page two.

3. Teacher Yasmin read every reflection. Teacher Yasmin wrote a kind note.
4. Amal ______ (like / likes) the library page best of all.
Check yourself: 1. She 2. They 3. She 4. likes.

grammar.title: Asking Clear Questions with Who, What, Where and How (Units 2 and 6)

grammar.title: Describing and Comparing with Adjectives and -er Than (Units 4 and 5)

assignments.instructions:
Submit four things: the published six-page booklet, three chosen portfolio pieces with a reason for each, a recording of your two-minute presentation, and your final reflection with one goal for Year 3.
Marking guidance for the teacher. Award the 64 marks as follows.
Booklet, 24 marks: 4 marks for each of the six pages. Give 2 marks for two accurate sentences, 1 mark for a matching picture and 1 mark for a correct label.
Portfolio choice, 12 marks: 4 marks for each piece, awarded for naming the unit, naming the skill and giving a real reason.
Presentation, 16 marks: use the Speaking rubric criteria of clarity, vocabulary, sentence accuracy and interaction, 4 marks each.
Reflection, 12 marks: 4 marks for a past sentence with -ed, 4 marks for a present sentence with -ing, and 4 marks for a future goal with will.
Do not award marks for drawing skill or for the materials a family can afford. Assess the English only, and accept scribed or recorded work where a learner needs it.

teacherNotes.note:
This unit revises Year 2. Use the map below when you confer with a learner, so the child can name where each idea came from.
Vocabulary groups: group 1 revises Unit 1 (name, partner, like, spell); group 2 revises Unit 2 (neighbour, window cleaner, police officer, reporter); group 3 revises Unit 3 (head, arm, hand, finger); group 4 revises Unit 4 (shadow, light, sun); group 5 revises Unit 5 (ten, twenty, thirty); group 6 revises Unit 6 (butterfly, cricket, ant); group 7 revises Unit 7 (planting, watering, picking up); group 8 revises Unit 8 (house, flat, hut); group 9 revises Unit 9 (library, shopping centre, underground).
Grammar workshops: Grammar 1 revises Units 1 and 9 (pronouns, like and likes); Grammar 2 revises Units 2 and 6 (question words and question marks); Grammar 3 revises Unit 3 (commands); Grammar 4 revises Units 4 and 5 (adjectives and -er than); Grammar 5 revises Units 6 and 8 (There is, There are and place words); Grammar 6 revises Units 4, 7, 8 and 9 (past -ed, present -ing and future will).
Cast: Amal is the same Grade 2 girl the class has followed since Unit 1. Teacher Yasmin, Nora, Leo, Sami, Maya, Daniel and Theo keep the roles they held all year, as do Adam and Idris (Amal's brothers), Mina (her sister), Grandma Hana, Omar the shopkeeper, Karim the window cleaner, Rami the police officer and Leila the firefighter. Never swap a role between names.
Treat the capstone as supported independent performance. Confer briefly with each learner, keep the child's own language on the page, and give one strength and one manageable next step.

grownUpGuide.label: Teacher & Parent Guide
grownUpGuide.intro: In this unit, your child works through "My English World: Grade 2 Capstone" — new words, a grammar focus, and a story. See exactly what they will practise below.

sections.title: 🧭 About this unit (please read first)
sections.body:
Your child is about 6-7 years old and is building on English they already know. So YOU lead this unit alongside them — a teacher in class or a parent at home.

Work in short, regular sessions rather than one long one. Reading together, saying words out loud, and playing with the grammar patterns matter more than getting every answer right first time.

This guide tells you what the unit covers and how to go through it together. The learner's own pages (Reading & story, Grammar, Activities) are what your child works through on screen.

sections.title: 💬 Using the AI Tutor with your child
sections.body:
The AI Tutor is there for extra practice and conversation — a grown-up should still be nearby, especially the first few times.

Ask the tutor to say a word slowly so your child can copy it: "Please say the word 'name' slowly."

Ask it to make up a short question using this unit's words, or to listen to your child's sentence and say if it sounds right.

Ask it for one more practice question if your child wants to keep going after the unit is finished.

sections.title: 🌟 Tips for teaching this unit
sections.body:
Keep sessions short and positive. Stop while it is still enjoyable, not after it has become a chore.

Say new words and example sentences out loud yourselves — hearing English spoken, not just reading it, is what builds confidence.

Let your child make mistakes without worrying. Gently model the correct version rather than correcting every slip.

Praise effort and progress, not just correct answers — confidence carries a learner further than perfect grammar at this stage.

sections.title: What Your Child Will Be Able to Do
items: Select and use review vocabulary from all nine Grade 2 units accurately in speech and in writing.
Read and listen to the three capstone texts and answer questions using evidence from the text.
Use the six grammar patterns taught across Grade 2 accurately in connected speaking and writing.
Plan, rehearse and deliver a two-minute presentation about the finished booklet and answer a listener's question.
Plan, draft, revise and publish an illustrated six-page booklet with a clear beginning, middle and ending.
Give, receive and act on kind, specific feedback during a peer conference.
Select portfolio evidence, reflect on progress across the year and set one next English goal.

sections.title: How to Teach This Unit, Step by Step
sections.body:
Repeat this simple shape over one or two short sessions:

1. Warm-up (2-3 min)
Say hello in English together and ask what your child remembers from the last unit.

2. Learn the words (5-10 min)
Go through Unit 1 Review — Welcome and Calendar, Unit 2 Review — Good Neighbours and Jobs, Unit 3 Review — Ready, Steady, Go!, Unit 4 Review — The Big Sky, Unit 5 Review — Let's Measure, Unit 6 Review — All About Bugs, Unit 7 Review — The World Around Us, Unit 8 Review — Home, Sweet Home, Unit 9 Review — Let's Explore the City!, a few words at a time. Say each word, then have your child repeat it and use it in a short sentence.

3. Grammar and practice (5-10 min)
Look at "Pronouns and Likes (Units 1 and 9)" together and try a few lines of its practice out loud.

4. Story and listening time (5 min)
Read or listen to "Amal's English Year" together, and enjoy "Showcase Day" too.

5. Activity time (5-10 min)
Sit with your child and do "Activity 1 — Portfolio Treasure Hunt" together, reading each instruction aloud for them if needed.

6. Wrap-up (2 min)
Ask what they learned today and celebrate with a “Well done!”

items: Amal presents her booklet. She points at page four.

Look at page one first.

There is one booklet on the table.
Last term I planted a tree with Adam.

sections.title: Simple Check — What to Look For
sections.body: You do not need a test. Just watch for these as you go through the unit together:
items: Thirty review words used correctly in the word bank (Writing 2), the booklet pages and the Vocabulary Spotlight recording (Speaking 2).
Twelve comprehension answers that quote a named person, page or detail from the story, the project brief or the showcase dialogue.
Six completed grammar workshops plus the ten-question cumulative quiz, and correct patterns in the published booklet.
The Speaking 6 recording from the showcase, timed at about two minutes, with one answered question from a visitor.
The plan (Writing 1), the marked draft (Writing 3), the revised copy (Writing 4) and the published booklet (Writing 5).
The completed feedback slip from Activity 4 and at least two named changes made to the draft in Writing 4.
Three chosen portfolio pieces with a reason for each, plus the final reflection naming one goal for Year 3.
